subject: physics
question_text: What is the discovery of C.V. Raman?

verification.note: Asked in TS Inter I-Year Physics Paper-I, March 2017 (Q1) and March 2020 (Q1) — Section A, 2 marks each time. The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question text itself is sourced from those papers. `appearances` is deliberately left empty — a separate reviewed tagging pass fills it, and a hand-written tag here would be an invented claim. Content hand-checked against NCERT Class-11 Chapter 1: C. V. Raman discovered the Raman effect, the scattering of light by molecules in which a small part of the scattered light emerges with a changed wavelength, and was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1930.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.margin_note: First mark. Name the effect, then say what changes in it.
steps.why: The question asks for a discovery, so it needs a name and one line saying what that name means. The change in wavelength is the whole content, because ordinary scattering leaves the wavelength unchanged.
common_mistakes: Naming the effect without saying what it is. The words change in wavelength carry the mark.

recall.must_convey: That C V Raman discovered the Raman effect, the scattering of light with a change in wavelength.

steps.memory_tip: Raman scattering changes the wavelength of the scattered light. Ordinary scattering does not.

lines.text: Raman effect · Nobel Prize in Physics, 1930

steps.margin_note: Second mark. Say WHY the wavelength changes: energy is exchanged with the molecule.
steps.why: The shifted wavelengths are the evidence. The light exchanges a fixed amount of energy with a molecule, so the size of the shift measures that molecule's own energy levels, and the effect became a tool for studying molecular structure.
common_mistakes: Saying all the scattered light changes wavelength. Only a small part of it does.
Saying the frequency of the light stays the same. A changed wavelength means a changed frequency.

recall.must_convey: That a small part of the scattered light comes out with a longer or shorter wavelength because energy is exchanged with the molecule.
accept: small part of the scattered light
energy is exchanged with the molecule

steps.memory_tip: Energy given to the molecule makes the light redder; energy taken from it makes the light bluer.

insider_note: One mark names the effect and the other says what it is — the name written alone, with no mention of the change in wavelength, is half.
